title: Joint Identified Sets for Stratum Effects in Instrumental Variable Models under Mechanism Invariance
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: the restricted finite-binary scope and limited practical evidence keep the package below field significance; math and decision reviews pass.
gap_reasons: The genuinely new content is confined to the finite-binary outcome-only shared-treatment-response elimination; the neither/both cases are direct coupling consequences, while the treatment-only branch is imported from Richardson–Robins.

The paper remains confined to binary variables, finite-support S, and full response-margin invariance, and it supplies neither sampling inference nor an applied analysis demonstrating how often the tightening matters beyond its constructed positive-cell witness.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved an exact outcome-only identified hyperrectangle under a shared treatment-response margin, sharp signed linear images, observable equality criteria, simultaneous finite attainment, and the resulting restricted four-mask synthesis. Independent math and decision reviews ultimately passed with no findings, but field-tier novelty failed because the other branches are classical or direct and the package lacks broader scope, inference, or applied evidence; those extensions remain separate future research topics.
tldr: The exact joint identified set of the stratum effects has one of four forms under either the response-margin class \(\mathcal C_M\) or its projection-equivalent root-exogenous SCM representation \(\mathcal P_M\): a common-effect diagonal \(\{(r)_s:r\in[BP^-,BP^+]\}\) when neither mechanism depends on \(S\); the sharp outcome-only hyperrectangle \(\prod_s[\ell_s(t_*),u_s(t_*)]\); the Richardson--Robins common-effect diagonal \(\{(r)_s:r\in I_X(q)\}\) when only the treatment mechanism depends on \(S\); and the unrestricted product \(\prod_s[BP_s^-,BP_s^+]\) when both mechanisms may depend on \(S\). Every point is finitely attained. As a corollary, averaging conditional Balke--Pearl bounds is universally sharp exactly for the neither and both masks when \(|\mathcal K|\geq2\), while both singleton masks fail by strict positive-cell witnesses. Novelty is claimed only for the outcome-only shared-treatment-response region and the restricted four-mask synthesis; the treatment-only interval remains fully credited to Richardson--Robins.
gap: Pointwise Balke--Pearl sharpness does not ensure that one latent response law attains all conditional endpoints. Jonzon et al. (2025), Proposition 3 and Corollary 1, establish validity for every mask but not mask-specific sharpness; Levis et al. (2025) solve a broader conditional-IV model without mechanism invariance; and Richardson--Robins solve the treatment-only multilevel-IV branch. The inspected sources do not characterize the cross-stratum restriction created when only the treatment response mechanism must remain invariant.
fill: Prove the shared-response-margin gluing characterization, the outcome-only compatibility and endpoint formulas with finite attaining SCMs, equality criteria and a sign-identifying witness; then combine these with the credited Richardson--Robins multilevel-IV branch to establish the four-mask theorem.
